findings.evidence: The summary claims constant invariance and says mean-zero solvability replaces coercivity when integral_Omega f != 0. Direct expansion gives I(u+c)=I(u)-c integral_Omega f, so invariance holds precisely for zero mean. If the mean is nonzero, arbitrarily small constants lower the energy and the homogeneous Neumann problem has no solution; restricting the solution to mean zero does not restore compatibility. The opened thm-weak-neumann-poisson-solvability-on-the-mean-zero-subspace requires F(1)=0 and records componentwise compatibility. Rewrite this B-page summary to distinguish zero-mean normalisation from incompatible forcing. B-page prose is outside the reader edit licence.

The sphere example additionally uses cor-weak-closure-of-the-unit-sphere-is-the-closed-unit-ball, whose Statement explicitly assumes HB. findings.location: items/thm-sigma-finite-duality-for-bounded-functionals-on-l-p.md, Proof steps 1.1–3.1, especially line 60; Statement and Given contain no choice premise
findings.evidence: The opened L1 supplier lem-rn-densities-of-bounded-l-p-functionals-belong-to-l-q supplies a unique density class on each finite-measure piece. Step 3.1 then asserts a single measurable function agreeing a.e. with all those classes, without selecting their countably many representatives or proving a choice-free gluing result. Compatibility of quotient classes does not itself construct that representative. For q=infinity the same step also selects countably many null-set witnesses. No listed fact supplies that selection/gluing premise and no Countable Choice or stronger principle is assumed. Add an explicit choice premise and glue selected representatives on the disjoint layers X_n minus X_(n-1), or supply a proved gluing theorem under the actual hypotheses. This is a gap in the displayed proof, not a claim that the ZFC duality theorem is false. The assigned consumer reaches this published supplier through cor-ell-p-duality-by-counting-measure.

findings.location: items/thm-strong-separation-of-closed-and-compact-convex-sets.md, Statement lines 28–30 and Given line 34; Proof steps 1.1–3.1, lines 48–52
findings.evidence: Potential missing ambient hypothesis: neither Statement nor Given specifies that X is a real or complex normed space, yet the proof uses distance to C, norm balls, the operator norm and sup_{||b||<r} Re f(b)=r||f||. Closedness, compactness and convexity alone do not declare that metric/norm structure. The opened home page geometric-hahn-banach-and-convex-separation has no global ambient-space declaration. State the intended normed-space and topology assumptions explicitly, or provide an explicit inherited convention licensing these constructions. The intended normed-space argument is sound, and the assigned consumer does supply a real or complex normed X; the finding concerns the published supplier interface rather than a demonstrated failure in that application.
